claims.claim_text: CyTOF analysis of platelet-rich plasma from a subset of vaccinated young, Older (Comm), and Older (SNF) adults at primary vaccination (day 0) and days 2 and 7 after primary vaccination (day 2 and day 7) showed significantly higher platelet surface CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 in Older (Comm) versus young adults, whereas Older (SNF) levels were significantly lower than Older (Comm) and largely comparable to young adults.

source.quote: The levels of surface expression of all three proteins were significantly increased in platelets from Older (Comm), compared to young adults at day 0, 2, and 7, suggesting an age-associated increase in platelet activation. We expected that the Older (SNF) group might show similar or even increased expression of these activation markers. However, surface expression in Older (SNF) adults was significantly decreased compared to Older (Comm), with Older (SNF) activation marker surface expression comparable to that of platelets from young adults (with the exception of Day 0 CD62p expression in Older (SNF) adults, which was significantly higher compared to platelets from young adults) (Figure 5c,f ).

comparison.finding: At day 0, platelet surface CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 were significantly higher in Older (Comm) adults than in young adults.
At day 0, platelet surface CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 in Older (SNF) adults were significantly lower than in Older (Comm) adults.
At day 0, Older (SNF) adults had platelet activation marker surface expression largely comparable to young adults, except CD62p was significantly higher in Older (SNF) adults.
At day 2, platelet surface CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 were significantly higher in Older (Comm) adults than in young adults.
At day 2, platelet surface CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 in Older (SNF) adults were significantly lower than in Older (Comm) adults.
At day 2, platelet surface CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 in Older (SNF) adults were largely comparable to young adults.
At day 7, platelet surface CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 were significantly higher in Older (Comm) adults than in young adults.
At day 7, platelet surface CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 in Older (SNF) adults were significantly lower than in Older (Comm) adults.
At day 7, platelet surface CD62p, CD40L, and CD63 in Older (SNF) adults were largely comparable to young adults.

claims.claim_text: RNA sequencing analysis of platelet-rich plasma from 28 young, 20 Older (Comm), and 17 Older (SNF) adults collected before primary vaccination (day 0) and days 2, 7, and 28 after primary vaccination (day 2, day 7, and day 28) showed age- and frailty-associated platelet activation signatures, with PF4 and PPBP and platelet activation pathways increased from Young to Older (Comm) to Older (SNF), while translation-related RNAs decreased across the same groups.

source.quote: This analysis found 1508 RNAs that were significantly different when comparing Young to Older (Comm) adults, and 2209 RNAs that were significantly different when comparing Older (Comm) to Older (SNF) adults (|log2fc| >1.5, adj. p value <0.05, Table 2 ). Platelet activation pathways were significantly enriched in Older (Comm) compared with young adults, as were Rho GTPase effector pathways mediating the activation response (Aslan & McCarty, 2013 ) and mitochondrial genes (Table 2 , Extended Data Figure S2b ). Notably, activation pathways in platelets from Older (SNF) adults were also significantly increased compared to Older (Comm) adults.

comparison.finding: At day 0, platelet activation pathways, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased in Older (Comm) versus Young, while translation-related RNAs were decreased in Older (Comm) versus Young.
At day 0, platelet activation pathways, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased in Older (SNF) versus Older (Comm), while translation-related RNAs were decreased in Older (SNF) versus Older (Comm).
At day 0, platelet activation signatures, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased from Young to Older (SNF), while translation-related RNAs were decreased from Young to Older (SNF).
At day 2, platelet activation pathways, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased in Older (Comm) versus Young, while translation-related RNAs were decreased in Older (Comm) versus Young.
At day 2, platelet activation pathways, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased in Older (SNF) versus Older (Comm), while translation-related RNAs were decreased in Older (SNF) versus Older (Comm).
At day 2, platelet activation signatures, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased from Young to Older (SNF), while translation-related RNAs were decreased from Young to Older (SNF).
At day 7, platelet activation pathways, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased in Older (Comm) versus Young, while translation-related RNAs were decreased in Older (Comm) versus Young.
At day 7, platelet activation pathways, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased in Older (SNF) versus Older (Comm), while translation-related RNAs were decreased in Older (SNF) versus Older (Comm).
At day 7, platelet activation signatures, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased from Young to Older (SNF), while translation-related RNAs were decreased from Young to Older (SNF).
At day 28, platelet activation pathways, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased in Older (Comm) versus Young, while translation-related RNAs were decreased in Older (Comm) versus Young.
At day 28, platelet activation pathways, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased in Older (SNF) versus Older (Comm), while translation-related RNAs were decreased in Older (SNF) versus Older (Comm).
At day 28, platelet activation signatures, including PF4 and PPBP, were increased from Young to Older (SNF), while translation-related RNAs were decreased from Young to Older (SNF).
